assessments.claim: C-001: The no-semantics hypothesis is too broad; defined formats are a counterexample.
assessments.rationale: Sections 7.1-7.2.2 support this qualified correction. The brief omits vocabulary/default and syntax-only detail present in the source.
Abstract and section 1 state an assessment purpose, not empirical accuracy. The brief omits the non-normative Note status.

assessments.claim: C-003: Assessment can include the provenance record itself.
assessments.rationale: Section 2.2.2 addresses provenance of provenance. The brief omits that the cited overview is informative.

assessments.claim: C-004: RAMP should distinguish formal/reference checks from source-support judgment.
assessments.rationale: Reasonable design conclusion from the sources' scope; explicitly labeled inference, not a source-imposed RAMP requirement.

assessments.claim: RAMP can validate declared constraints and trace claims to recorded passages.
assessments.rationale: These sources establish conceptual tools, not implemented RAMP capability. No implementation demonstration was examined.

assessments.claim: The packet contains evidence IDs and source-section locators.
assessments.rationale: Directly observed in supplied evidence.json and sources.json; this does not establish source support by itself.

assessments.claim: The pilot does not establish general agent accuracy or comparative reliability.
assessments.rationale: A justified scope limitation for the supplied artifacts, which contain no general performance study.

modelAssistedSourceSupport.dispositionAssessment: Bounded-answer complete is defensible. Full-charter completeness remains unverified; the brief does not supply all acceptance records. Do not compare its bounded disposition directly to the other brief's full-charter disposition.
limitations: Source-status and informative-section qualifications are available through the packet but absent from the brief's own wording.
Present-tense RAMP capability needs implementation evidence or conditional wording.
Open questions preserve cross-topic transfer, human agreement and blinded repeated comparison; operational validator and snapshot questions are missing.

assessments.claim: Validation and format behavior depend on the applicable vocabulary and implementation configuration.
assessments.rationale: Sections 3 and 7 support the account. Refusal is required when Format-Assertion is declared true; required checks are syntactic, not existence/truth checks.

assessments.claim: Provenance supports assessment without a mere-record truth guarantee.
assessments.rationale: Abstract and section 1 support assessment; the brief correctly preserves the non-normative Note qualification.

assessments.claim: PROV models entities, activities, agents and provenance of provenance.
assessments.rationale: Sections 2.1 and 2.2.2 support this account. The Recommendation/informative-section distinction is correctly preserved.

assessments.claim: Keep conformance, preservation and source support separate; passing records may retain mistakes.
assessments.rationale: The brief explicitly marks the recommendation and hypothetical examples; these are not observed failures or a measured reliability result.

assessments.claim: Preserve the proposed configuration, claim, passage, transformation and review fields, and compare retained records separately from support review.
assessments.rationale: Useful proposed practice; the sources do not mandate this exact field set or demonstrate its effectiveness.

assessments.claim: Schema results and provenance can preserve an inspectable handoff account.
assessments.rationale: Defensible conceptual possibility; it does not establish that this handoff or RAMP implementation actually preserved the account.

assessments.claim: The brief used two cycles, exactly the packet URLs, no earlier access to the other condition and the reported tool exclusions.
assessments.rationale: Workflow self-reports cannot be verified from the three public sources or the brief itself. Execution history was not audited; no contradiction is established.

assessments.claim: The listed local/configuration hashes describe the actual inputs and configuration.
assessments.rationale: Not source-support claims; this reviewer did not recompute hashes or audit configuration provenance.

assessments.claim: Confidence is high in the narrow reading; effectiveness and comparison remain unmeasured.
assessments.rationale: High confidence is uncalibrated self-assessment. The explicit absence of measured effectiveness is appropriately preserved.

modelAssistedSourceSupport.dispositionAssessment: Partial against the full charter, with the bounded conceptual question answered, is appropriately scoped. This brief alone cannot certify integration, preservation or all acceptance records.
limitations: Workflow and hash assertions require separate audit evidence.
Operational validator, snapshot and human-adjudication questions are explicit; cross-topic transfer and blinded repetition are not explicit open questions.
More explicit qualifications in this artifact do not establish a causal improvement from role separation.
